title: Ecosystem adoption trigger catalog and buyer-timeline heatmap
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Summary: Build a reusable catalog of adoption triggers (technical and commercial) across model suppliers and vertical buyers, and produce a buyer-timeline heatmap that correlates triggers to procurement stages. This artifact will inform fallback policies, pricing experiments, and sales enablement for Dedicated/Private offerings.

Context: Current model-landscape tracking focuses on feature presence and latency/cost benchmarks, but we lack a structured mapping from observable signals (new quantization, regional availability, price cuts, SLA announcements, open-source forks) to when customers start procurement, evaluate, and decide. This makes it hard to prioritize which supplier events should generate internal signals and playbooks.

Goals:
- Define a taxonomy of adoption triggers (technical, commercial, regulatory, ecosystem).
- Map each trigger to an empirically-derived lead time window for buyer action (awareness -> evaluation -> procurement).
- Produce a heatmap that shows typical procurement stage shifts by industry vertical and company size.
- Recommend which triggers should create automated alerts in the model-scout pipeline and which require manual investigation.
- Deliver a three-slide executive summary and a living Confluence catalog with templates for signal entries.

Success metrics:
- Heatmap completed and validated with >12 customer interviews and 8 AE feedbacks.
- Signal-to-action rules defined for the top 20 supplier events covering >80% of observed switch cases.
- Playbook recommendations accepted by Sales Ops and Research.

Deliverables:
- Confluence: "Adoption Trigger Catalog" page (living).
- Heatmap CSV + interactive dashboard link (Runbook -> LookerBoard).
- Signal classification rubric (auto vs manual) and priority list.
- One-pager for Sales and Solutions with recommended play actions per trigger.

Key stakeholders:
- PM: Marco Chen (owner)
- Research lead: Lina Gómez
- Field: 3 AEs for interviews (Tom Park, Nadia Stephens, Alex Ruiz)
- Eng: runtime-data team for telemetry access (ENG-7312 contact: Priya Malhotra)
- Sales Ops: Iris Patel

Assumptions and constraints:
- We can access anonymized procurement timelines from 15 pilot customers under NDA for qualitative calibration.
- Some signals (e.g., leaked roadmap commits) will be noisy; we will require triangulation before automated alerts.
- This work prioritizes English-speaking NA/EU customers for Q2 due to resource constraints.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In scope: model supplier events, price changes, quant releases, regional GA announcements, SLA updates, security/compliance certifications, easy-to-detect open-source forks.
- Out of scope: deep vendor contract terms, legal negotiation playbooks, non-technical marketing campaigns (unless tied to product announcements).

Risks:
- Insufficient interview volume could skew lead-time estimates. Mitigation: couple interviews with anonymized telemetry and publicly recorded announcement dates.
- False positives in automated alerts may create noise for Solutions. Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds and manual verification step.

Acceptance criteria:
- Catalog page contains at least 40 discrete trigger entries with taxonomy labels.
- Heatmap includes at least 3 vertical slices (SaaS, fintech, regulated-enterprise) and two company-size buckets (SMB, Mid/Enterprise).
- Signal rules documented and demoed to Sales Ops with sign-off.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/trigger-catalog-draft (placeholder)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/market-playbooks/pull/198 (placeholder)
comments: 2026-02-12 — Initial kickoff: scoped taxonomy categories and assigned interviews to AEs. Action: Marco to schedule interview slots with 10 customers.

2026-02-20 — Research update: Lina delivered a preliminary list of 27 candidate triggers from desk research (pricing changes, quant releases, ISO certifications, region GA). Need to expand to ecosystem signals (partner integrations, vector DB compatibility announcements).
2026-02-28 — Eng sync: runtime-data team confirmed access to anonymized model-switch telemetry; ENG-7312 to provide sample dataset by 2026-03-05.

2026-03-05 — Customer interviews: 6 interviews completed; early pattern: price cuts and new regional GA have fastest downstream procurement signals; regulator certifications show longer lead times but higher conversion. Recommended adjusting heatmap buckets.
2026-03-10 — Draft heatmap: first pass uploaded to LookerBoard. Pending validation with Sales Ops and two additional AE interviews. Marco requested Sales Ops sign-off meeting (2026-03-15).

2026-03-12 — Scope decision: automated alerts will be limited to 8 high-confidence triggers for initial rollout (price change >10% downward, new GA in customer region, SLA published, major quantized model release). The rest will be manual-review-only.
notes: Follow-up: prepare a short survey for AEs post-interview to quantify CFU (customer follow-up urgency). Also include a small section on signature indicators that precede a vendor switch (e.g., public issue tracker activity, community forum spikes).
